$comment: Write-guard classification for Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL, shared by every binding. Sourced from the Azure Cosmos DB REST API reference (learn.microsoft.com/rest/api/cosmos-db/: common request headers, documents, stored procedures, triggers, transactional batch, patch, change feed and query plan) and the operation types the SDKs expose (Node @azure/cosmos OperationType, .NET and Java OperationType). The unit is the operation type; a hook that sees only the HTTP request derives the operation type with the rules under fromRequest. Anything not listed is a write. See spec/data-stores.md.
source: Azure Cosmos DB REST API reference (x-ms-version 2018-12-31 and later); SDK OperationType enums
keyFormat: The operation type name, compared case-insensitively and reported with the spelling below: Node's @azure/cosmos spells them in lower case (read, query, execute). Node's Execute is .NET and Java's ExecuteJavaScript, and Node's Query covers .NET's SqlQuery. Node sends its query-plan request as a read and its change-feed request as a query; both are reads either way.
rules: A request that names a pre-trigger or post-trigger (x-ms-documentdb-pre-trigger-include or x-ms-documentdb-post-trigger-include, the SDKs' preTriggerInclude and postTriggerInclude options) is a write whatever its operation type: triggers run only around writes, and their code can write.
Executing a stored procedure (Execute, ExecuteJavaScript) is a write, even when the procedure only reads: the guard can't see its code.
Batch is a write. It covers transactional batches and the SDKs' bulk mode, which sends batch requests with x-ms-cosmos-batch-atomic: false.
Patch is a write, including a conditional patch whose filter predicate fails.
Query, ReadFeed (including the change feed) and QueryPlan are reads: the Cosmos DB query language can't write.
Reading or querying databases, containers, offers, partition key ranges, stored procedures, triggers and user-defined functions is a read. Creating, replacing or deleting any of them is a write.
x-ms-cosmos-allow-tentative-writes is sent on every request, reads included, and says nothing about the operation.

fromRequest.$comment: For hooks on the HTTP pipeline (Python and Go policies), which see the request rather than the SDK's operation type. Header names are case-insensitive; boolean header values compare case-insensitively with True.
fromRequest.path: The resource path alternates resource types and ids: /dbs/{db}/colls/{coll}/docs/{doc}. A path with an even number of segments addresses one resource; an odd number addresses a feed of the last resource type. The root path / reads the database account.

order.operation: the derived type below, classified as a write

order.when: method GET, a feed or the account root
method POST and x-ms-documentdb-isquery: True, or Content-Type application/query+json
method POST on one resource under sprocs (/dbs/{db}/colls/{coll}/sprocs/{sproc})

order.operation: the method name, which is a write

fromRequest.target: db.collection.name is the container id: the segment after colls. db.namespace is the database id: the segment after dbs.

notes.Preview: Cosmos DB can only roll back inside one logical partition, through a transactional batch the client builds up front. An arbitrary handler's writes can't be held back and discarded, so Cosmos DB runs in guard mode only.
notes.Credentials: The authorization header (a master-key signature or an Entra ID token) and the account key are never captured.
